text:
acme-sre-raj: Hey team — we started seeing a mix of 429 and occasional 403 errors on /v1/generate from our staging fleet around 09:07 UTC. No app code changes; only infra churn (containers rebooting during deploy). Some containers succeed, others 429. Billing alerted about a sudden burst. Can someone help triage?

acme-sre-raj: Quick curl we ran from one failing container (key redacted):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ORG-REDACTED" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"gptx-lite","input":"hello"}'
```

acme-sre-raj: Response headers we captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 59
content-type: application/json
```

support-jess: Thanks — couple quick Qs: is that token an org-scoped token (created at org level) or a project-scoped key? Are you NATing multiple containers behind one public IP?

acme-sre-raj: It's an org-scoped key (we created a single token for all CI and staging projects to simplify creds). Our staging runs on EKS and most pods egress via a single NAT GW public IP that spikes on deploy.

eng-infra-tyler: Noted. Two separate blunt instruments can bite you here: org-level quotas and the egress-IP burst guard. Org keys aggregate usage across projects and count against org quota; if many pods burst at once you'll exhaust the org token bucket quickly. Separately, our platform has an IP burst guard to mitigate noisy tenants collapsing on a single IP. The headers you pasted are the token-level window but they won't always show IP-burst state.

acme-sre-raj: Interesting — how can we tell which enforcement triggered the 429 (org vs ip vs project)? The body returned a trace id: txn_ff4b9a2c in one sample.

support-jess: If the JSON error body includes type "rate_limit_exceeded" and trace_id, paste it and we can map it to internal logs. Also, if per-key headers show remaining >0 but you still get 429s, that's usually the ip-guard or org throttle acting outside the key window.

acme-sre-raj: Sample body:
```
{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Rate limit exceeded","trace_id":"txn_ff4b9a2c"}}
```

eng-infra-tyler: We'll look up txn_ff4b9a2c. Quick diagnostic steps for you: 1) run the small staggered startup test (start N/10 pods then add the rest) to see if it's bursty-start behavior; 2) run from a single pod repeated requests and capture headers; 3) run `curl -I https://api.redwood-inference.com/status` to ensure requests are hitting the same egress IP you expect.

support-jess: Mitigations while we investigate:
- Create project-scoped keys and distribute per-service so you spread quotas;
- Smooth startup with client-side token bucket or randomized jitter;
- Ask us for a temporary IP burst exception (we can escalate to infra for a 30–60 minute window).

acme-sre-raj: Question on billing — our billing dashboard shows a spike but then refunded-looking adjustments. Could an org-level key usage across many projects attribute unexpected usage to one project or to org-level billing?

billing-lina: Org-managed keys can make attribution trickier. Usage is attributed to the project context supplied in the request (if any) but if requests omit project headers, fallback attribution can be the org default. We can check the request metadata for org/project fields tied to txn_ff4b9a2c and reconcile charges. If you want to avoid accidental cross-project billing, use project-scoped keys.

acme-sre-raj: Repro: I did two runs today —
- Run A (all 120 pods boot at once): 35% immediate 429 and increased billing spike.
- Run B (staggered over 90s): zero 429s.

eng-infra-tyler: That matches a token-bucket burst exhaustion. Important nuance: org-scoped keys often have a larger bucket but also larger refill windows depending on plan; they can still throw 429s when aggregate usage exceeds refill. The IP guard acts as a safety net and can short-circuit even if token says remaining > 0.

support-jess: Next steps from our side:
- We will correlate txn_ff4b9a2c in infra logs and return whether the 429 was attributed to ip-guard or org quota.
- Platform-oncall-bot will open RW-80211 for infra to review NAT IP behavior.
- I recommend you create at least two project-scoped keys: one for CI agents (low rate) and one per critical service (or per N containers) during rollout.

platform-oncall-bot: Created RW-80211 and assigned to infra-oncall. Tags: rate-limit, ip-guard, billing.

billing-lina: If you prefer immediate protection from accidental charges, we can also place a hard stop on the staging project's billing to prevent further overage (this will cause additional 429s when quota hit). Let me know if you want us to enable that for proj-staging-41.

acme-sre-raj: For now please do NOT hard-stop; we need the pipeline to finish. Please proceed with the infra lookup and temporary IP exception while we implement jitter.

eng-infra-tyler: We found txn_ff4b9a2c — enforcement source: IP_BURST_GUARD. We also see several adjacent traces from other projects using the same org token. Infra can lift IP guard for your NAT for a 45-minute window.

support-jess: Raj — confirm public egress IP and desired window. Also we'll add a short doc link to the best-practices page on keys and burst handling.

acme-sre-raj: Public IP is 18.205.34.102. Please grant 45 minutes. Also creating project keys now.

platform-oncall-bot: IP exception requested for 18.205.34.102, duration 45 minutes, ticket RW-80211 updated.

support-jess: Follow-ups and recommendations posted to RW-80211: distribute keys, add startup jitter, implement client-side leaky-bucket to smooth N requests/sec, consider Dedicated if sustained concurrency required, and prefer project-scoped keys for better billing attribution.

billing-lina: We'll reconcile the billing spike with infra after the window and offer to credit any clearly platform-side misattribution within reason.

acme-sre-raj: Thanks all — rotating keys and adding jitter now. I'll report back if we still hit 429s after rotation. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:
